title: Local iloprost therapy to promote bone healing in high risk fractures
official: PRECISION Study: A phase II prospective, mono-center, randomized, double-blinded, controlled trial to assess the efficacy of local iloprost therapy to promote bone healing in patients at risk for fracture non-union
summary: Main objective: To evaluate whether a single, local dose of iloprost at the fracture site improves bone healing in patients identified as being at high risk of impaired fracture healing based on elevated pre-operative CD8+ T effector memory cells re-expressing CD45RA (TEMRA) levels.
conditions: bone fracture in patients identified as being at high risk of impaired fracture healing based on elevated pre-operative CD8+ T effector memory cells re-expressing CD45RA (TEMRA) levels

interventions.name: Ilomedin® 20 μg/1 ml, Konzentrat zur Herstellung einer Infusionslösung

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Signed written informed consent prior to any study-specific procedures.
2. 2.	Male or female patient aged 18 to 80 years at the time of screening.
3. 3.	Acute fracture not older than 10 days at screening.
4. 4.	Eligible fracture according to AO classification: a. Clavicle (15.2 A-C); b. Humerus (11A2, 12A-C, 13A2-3); c. Radius (2R2A-C); d. Ulna (2U2A-C); e. Femur (31A3, 32A-C, 33A2-3); f. Tibia (41A2-3, 42A-C, 43A1-3)
5. 5.	Planned treatment by ORIF.
6. 6.	CD8+ TEMRA-high immune profile defined as ≥38% late-stage effector memory CD3+CD8+CD57+CD28− T cells among total CD8+ T cells in peripheral blood.
7. 7.	In patients with multiple eligible fractures, the fracture with the highest AO complexity (A=low -C=high) will be selected for study evaluation.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.	Inability to provide informed consent.
2. 2.	Immunosuppression due to disease or medication.
3. 3.	Current malignancy requiring chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, or other active treatment.
4. 4.	Hypersensitivity to iloprost or any excipient.
5. 5.	Conditions associated with increased bleeding risk due to platelet inhibition, including active peptic ulcer disease or intracranial hemorrhage.
